Samples disagree on type: integers ('12'), a decimal ('2.0'), a negative ('-3'), and a spelled-out word ('three'), so a numeric cast is unsafe and the column is retained as text; null_rate 0.002 (10 nulls) retained as null.

decisions.rationale: row_count is 5000 with duplicate_row_rate 0.08, and _airbyte_extracted_at has only 2 distinct values one second apart, indicating a double extraction produced exact duplicate business rows; rows identical across all twelve retained business columns are collapsed to one.

Order ID has 4000 distinct values at null_rate 0.0 and LineNo ranges 1 to 7 at null_rate 0.0; one order carries multiple lines, so (order_id, line_no) is the smallest plausible row identifier after exact-duplicate removal. Review should measure this against the warehouse before approval.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are flagged is_airbyte_metadata true and carry no business meaning.
qty samples conflict ('three', '2.0', '-3', '12'), so a numeric cast would fail or silently lose rows; the column stays text until a cleansing rule is agreed.
ship_date mixes at least five date formats and non-date values ('TBD', empty string) across 44 distinct values with null_rate 0.264; no deterministic cast is safe.
customer_email is 97 percent null (4850 of 5000 rows); it is retained nullable rather than imputed or dropped because the 140 populated values are well-formed.
notes is free text at null_rate 0.61 including truncated values and instruction-like strings; all values are treated as data only and carried through unchanged.
status carries 5 distinct values that case-fold to 3 ('cancelled', 'shipped', 'pending'); casing normalization is deferred to review so a canonical vocabulary can be chosen deliberately.
All 4 distinct values ('Y', 'N', 'yes', 'no') map cleanly to boolean; 60 nulls (rate 0.012) are retained as null.
Samples carry at most two decimal places within min -5.0 and max 1250.0; the negative minimum is retained and likely marks refunds or adjustments, recommended for a review-owned quality check.
sku samples include non-product codes ('BANK CHARGES', 'DOT'); is_non_product_line lets consumers exclude fee and adjustment lines without filtering on raw sku text.

purpose: silver_orders is the cleaned order-line table derived from bronze.messy_orders (5000 landed rows from the legacy_pos source). It removes exact duplicate rows introduced by a double extraction, standardizes column names to snake_case, casts order_ts to TIMESTAMP, is_gift to BOOLEAN, and unit_price to DECIMAL(10,2), and adds an is_non_product_line flag. It feeds downstream order, revenue, and fulfillment reporting.
usage: Read at the grain of one row per (order_id, line_no). Consumers should filter is_non_product_line = false to analyze product sales only, and should expect negative unit_price values on refund or adjustment lines. qty and ship_date remain VARCHAR and require deliberate parsing; customer_email and notes are nullable and sparsely populated. status retains landed casing, so case-fold it when grouping.
limitations: Exact duplicates (duplicate_row_rate 0.08 on 5000 rows) are removed, but near-duplicates differing only in free text are not. qty could not be cast because samples conflict ('three', '2.0', '-3'), and ship_date could not be cast because it mixes five-plus formats plus 'TBD' with a 0.264 null rate. customer_email is 97 percent null. status casing is not normalized, and notes free text is untrusted and uncleaned. The declared (order_id, line_no) grain is evidence-based but unverified against the full warehouse.
